transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to discuss the Northstar Systems royalty audit matter. As we all know, our license agreement with Northstar permits a royalty audit when reporting discrepancies are identified, and their quarterly reports have been showing inconsistent usage figures. The commercial team wants this handled without disrupting the existing license. Before I can approve any enforcement plan or authorize formal notice to Northstar, I need input from each of you per our weekly enforcement-review procedure. So let's hear from finance, IP, privacy, and account counsel -- what are your respective assessments and recommendations?

I had not yet circulated these notice requirements, so everyone should be aware of these constraints as we formulate the enforcement plan.

transcript.text: I need to share an important privacy constraint for the audit. I confirmed with Northstar's privacy lead that the audit materials include EU employee-level usage records. The approved method is an on-site review using pseudonymized records, with no export of EU employee data -- rather than a remote transfer of the raw files. This means our enforcement plan needs to account for an on-site audit process and cannot simply request remote transfer of the underlying data.
